title: AI Stocks in Focus as SAP Weighs 10,000 Job Cuts
summary: SAP is weighing at least 10,000 job cuts in an AI-driven restructuring, Bloomberg reported, as Nvidia and Alphabet slid on AI spending worries.
body_markdown:
Founded in 1972, SAP develops enterprise resource planning systems, and it has adapted to the AI era with agentic tools such as its Joule and Business AI platforms, Investing.com noted.


## Nvidia (NVDA): Slumps 4% as AI Stocks Sell Off


Nvidia slumped 4% on Wednesday after notching one of its best days on record on Monday, according to[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/25/nvidia-ai-stock-tech-selloff.html) . Jensen Huang's return to the company on Monday briefly revived appetite for tech stocks but did not fully calm concerns over the high costs tied to the AI build-out and worries of a potential slowdown, CNBC reported.


Semiconductor stocks dragged on the index in[Wednesday's session](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/stock-market-today-nov-25-2026-close/) , as the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite declined 0.6% and the VanEck Semiconductor ETF edged down 1%. Micron Technology fell 4%, while a hot inflation reading fueled concerns that higher interest rates could dent demand for growth stocks, including tech, per CNBC.


> "We just feel that this is panic right now," Venu Krishna, head of U.S. equity strategy at Barclays, told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street," adding that the market is telling investors "the AI growth narrative has hit a wall."


## Alphabet (GOOGL): Google Sets Usage Tiers for AI Agents


Alphabet and Amazon each declined about 2% on Wednesday, CNBC reported.[Technology stocks](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-invest-in-technology-stocks-a-5-step-plan/) fell as excitement over Huang's return to Nvidia faded and failed to calm concerns over the sustainability of the AI trade, according to the same report.


Separately, Google launched new usage tiers on Nov. 24 for AI agents that reach Gmail, Calendar, Drive and other Workspace products through its Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, according to[Google for Developers](https://developers.google.com/workspace/tools-safety) . The free Standard Tier covers up to 5,000 requests per day, per project, per product, and Google expects less than 1% of active Workspace developers to need to move beyond it. The dates below come from the same Google page.


Date Google Workspace change for AI agents


Nov. 24, 2026 Standard and Scaled Tiers launch across 8 MCP servers, including Gmail, Calendar and Drive


Feb. 1, 2027 AI agents must use Google Workspace MCP servers or the Google Workspace CLI


Apr. 1, 2027 Scaled Tier billing takes effect; Gmail, Calendar and Drive MCP usage is billed from the first request


From Feb. 1, 2027, agents that keep calling Workspace REST APIs directly will be limited to Standard Tier quotas, regardless of the tier their project selects, Google said.
